All Serb cultural institutions were also banned, and all Serbs had to declare the property they possessed in the independent state of Croatia. This property was later confiscated. Serbs just like Jews had to wear a band on their arm sleeve indicating that they were Orthodox. The new authorities of Franjo Tudjman throughout 1990 and 1991 created an atmosphere in which just like during the independent state of Croatia, it was possible for various establishments to put up signs saying, "Serbs prohibited from entering this establishment." In the independent state of Croatia, this prohibition also applied to Jews and Romas. The new leadership of Croatia in 1990 and 1991 not only accepted the values of the independent state of Croatia and applied Ustasha methods but they also used identical symbols. They introduced a new Croatian symbols, the checkered flag which was the flag that flew during the time when hundreds of thousands of Serbs died during the Second World War. The term for policeman was the same one as the one used during the independent state of Croatia. They also erected monuments to the worst criminals from the Second World War, throws who killed the most Serbs. The units of Croatian army were named after the names or named after war criminals from the Second World War. As for the Croatian army, I should really refer to it as the paramilitary because that's what it was. What Serbs did in Croatia was an attempt to self-organise and to try to protect them through democratic means. Serbs used amendments to request that the Serbs be reinstated as a constitutive nation. However, this was something that the Croatian parliament refused in 1990. Serbs warned that the secession of Croatia was anti-constitutional, represented a crime, based on the international law. However, Croatian authorities disregarded this just like many other signals, and they became more and more brutal in their attitude towards Serbs, instituting a process to convert Serb children into Catholicism, which is a form of genocide. The new government of Croatia did not respect the OECD declaration, which was adopted on the 19th of July 1991, which supported unity and territorial integrity of Yugoslavia. Croatia disregarded international law and recommendations given by the Conference on Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe and, contrary to these recommendations, carried out a secret process of arming various units which used fascist greetings and fascist symbols. Serbs were beaten, intimidated, their houses were mined and destroyed throughout 1990 and 1991. The Serbs in Croatia responded to this attitude of Croatian government by showing their support for preservation of Yugoslavia as a federal state with existing federal units. The Serbs demanded to have their own cultural autonomy within the Republic of Croatia. We are talking here about the cultural autonomy. In the case of disintegration of the Yugoslav state, the Serbs in Krajina wanted the same principle to be applied as the principle used for self-determination of Croats and Slovenes. They wanted the same benefit to apply to them within Croatia. The Serbs in Krajina, within their ethnic territory, wanted the protection for themselves both territorial and institutional. However, Croatian government displayed arrogance and disregarded these requests, responding to them through antidemocrat measures. The Serbs in Croatia established a community of municipalities where there was a majority of Serb population. This was envisaged in the constitution of the Republic of Croatia; however, Croatia prevented this establishment by unlawful and forcible means. After Croatian authorities refused all attempts of Serbs to organise and harmonise these relations within Croatia, Serbs decided, in order to protect themselves, to establish within their ethnic territory the SAO Krajina and, later on, the Serbian Republic of Krajina in 1991. It was then that Croatia began an undeclared war against Serbs living in the Serbian Republic of Krajina, which previously was known as SAO Krajina. When pursuant to the resolution of the Security Council of 1991, the territories populated by Serbs in Croatia were placed under the protection of the UN, and when, in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Krajina in 1992, the peace forces of the UN known as UNPROFOR arrived, in that area, just like in the territory throughout the Republic of Croatia, the Yugoslav army withdrew in accordance with the Vance-Owen plan. The territory of the Serbian Republic of Krajina became a territory protected by the UN, where federal regulations were supposed to be applied, those of Yugoslavia, not regulations of Croatia. This is what Vance Plan stipulated. The objective of deploying UN forces in Yugoslavia in Croatian territory where Serbs constituted a majority or a significant minority, and in which ethnic tension led to conflicts prior to that, was precisely to create conditions for negotiations on a peaceful resolution of the Yugoslav crisis without forecasting its outcome. Local police of the Krajina Serbs was recognised by Vance Plan and Security Council resolution establishing the UN mission in Yugoslavia. It was recognised as police which was supposed to act in the protected area under the control of the international forces. Territorial Defence of Krajina, of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, was demobilised in accordance with the Vance Plan. Their weapons were placed under double key in UN depots. The Serbs from Krajina accepted Vance Plan. They implemented this plan, just like the authorities of Yugoslavia did, the authorities which created all the conditions necessary for the arrival of international forces following which the JNA forces withdrew from that territory. However, the expectations of the Serbian people in the Republic of Serbian Krajina that the forces of the UN would protect them were not met. Even before the forces of the UN were fully deployed, Croatia carried out an aggression against the protected area. This took place at the Miljevacki Plateau on the 21st of June 1992. It was then that 40 members of the Serbian Territorial Defence were brutally killed. After they butchered them they were thrown into ditches. Their remains were removed in the presence of international observers. This behaviour of Croatian authorities which in 1992 not only attacked the area protected by the UN but also refused to implement the UN resolution 762 dated the 26th of June 1992, demanding them to withdraw from this territory, but just like the Ustashas in the Second World War, they dumped the killed Serbs into ditches. At the meeting of the military leadership of Croatia in March of 1992, the president of Croatia, General Tudjman, explained that Croatia has achieved a miracle. It created an army, I'm now quoting him, "numbering 200.000 people, together with police," and it was this military force that enabled Croatia to violate all norms of international law and all requests of the international community. In January 1993, Croatian army launched a new aggression against the UN-protected area. They did so by carrying out an operation called Maslenica. It was begun on the 22nd of January 1993. In a front which was almost 100 kilometres broad, they attacked from the south of the -- of the Serbian Republic of Krajina. It was on that occasion that Croatia seized a large piece of territory in Kotari and took control of the Peruca hydropower station. A lot of Serbs were killed during that operation in Serbian villages, Smokovic, Kasic, Zemunic Donji, and other villages where Serbs from ethnically mixed villages, for example, Murvica, Zemunic Gornji, Police were either deported or killed, their property destroyed and churches wrecked. Hundreds of Serbian civilians perished in this aggression. A lot of them were deported, whereas UN resolution 802 dated the 25th of January 1993 stipulating that Croatian forces need to withdraw was disregarded by Croatia. All of this was taking place up until mid-1993, at which time the second general of the UN, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, reported on the 15th of May 1993, to the UN Security Council that a pogrom had been carried out against Serbs in Croatia. He stated on that occasion that 251.000 Serbs were expelled from Croatia only until the 18th of March 1993. This involved the Serbs who, under the terror carried out by Croatian authorities had to leave their homes, flats and their employments in Croatia outside of the territory of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, which is to say outside of the territory under UN protection. There were no armed conflicts in those areas and the Serb population was expelled from there only because of their ethnicity. The Security Council was speechless upon hearing this. Logically, this resulted in a new act of aggression by Croatia committed in the area of the Medak pocket on the 9th of September 1993. On this occasion, three Serb villages were totally destroyed, Divoselo, Citluk, and Pocitelj. 88 Serbs were killed or went missing, mostly civilians. The Croatian side in mid-September surrendered to the Serb side a total of 52 bodies. UNPROFOR managed to retrieve another 18. Another two were retrieved by members of the Serbian Krajina and one last body was found as late as April 1995. High UNPROFOR officials back in 1993 conveyed to the leaders of the Serbian Krajina messages from the Croatian authorities and leaders, more specifically General Janko Bobetko, head of the General Staff, supreme staff, the Croatian army. I quote, "Tell the Serbs that the long Croatian arm will eventually catch up with them." These were messages that an OTP witness spoke about, Mr. Charles Kirudja. These were messages passed on to the Serbs before the Medak pocket operation. What was this message by the Croatian authorities supposed to mean? This has been explained by an UNPROFOR General Jan Kott who on the 19th of September 1993, visited the area and stated as follows. I quote, "I have found no signs of life or people or animals on my way through several villages that we passed. Destruction was total, systematic, and deliberate." There were no Serbs -- Serb prisoners. Either they escaped or they were dead. Mr. Kirudja spoke about the protest that he launched with the Croatian authorities over their racist attitude, of the racist attitude of the Croatian military and government, to the members of the Kenyan battalion of UNPROFOR. The same thing was reiterated by General Satish Nambiar and General Eraprop [phoen]. If Tudjman's Croatian government found it difficult to put up with armed members of UNPROFOR, if they belonged to the wrong ethnic background or religious background, it was quite clear that what lay in store for the Serbs was an unprecedented disaster. As early as 1992 the Croatian President Franjo Tudjman stated as follows. I quote: "There would have been no war had Croatia not wanted one." That same year, the Croatian president, General Tudjman, took the floor at a meeting of the Croatian leadership and said that the Croatia -- that Croatia only accepted the peacekeeping forces in order to avoid further material destruction and, even more importantly, to be granted international recognition. He said they with would use the presence of peacekeeping forces to prepare their own military units. This was precisely what Croatia ended up doing. All the while, it kept accusing the Krajina Serbs of a lack of cooperation, failure to cooperate, and of acts of aggression. All the while, all the Serbs were doing were just remaining on their own land, trying to get themselves organised and enjoy the international protection from a massacre that was in the offing and about to be committed by the Croatian forces. Every attempt to reach a political solution was interrupted and dismantled by Croatia while creating an appearance of political cooperation. Just like the cease-fire agreement signed on the British ship Avenger in September 1993 was used to put a stop to the operations in the Medak pocket, likewise on the 1st of January 1995, on the 1st of May 1995, the Croatian government violated the Zagreb agreement from 1994 to cease all hostilities and again attacked a UN-protected area. On the 1st of May 1995, the Croatian army and police forces launched a synchronised attack on Western Slavonia, UNPROFOR soldiers had been given advance notice and simply let the Croatian soldiers through. The Croatian soldiers only took several days to seize the entire area. Following this act of aggression, barely 800 Serbs remained of the original 22.000 living in the area. Over a span of several days, 284 civilians were killed, 57 of whom were women and eight were children. About 1400 members of the Serbian army were taken prisoner. Whole columns of scared Serbian folk were passing by. They were fleeing Western Slavonia and seized by panic on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd of 1995, these people tried to seek shelter in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They were fired at by heavy artillery from all sides, fired at by the Croatian police and army. This was a veritable massacre. Unprotected civilians on horse-drawn carts, vans, and lorries, were fired at by mortars, hand-held rocket launchers, and even bombed by Croatian planes. All the leaders of the Serbian Krajina appealed to the special envoy of the Secretary-General of the United Nations, Yasushi Akashi to stop this massacre, but the Croatian authorities failed to respond in any way. The OTP believes that I am responsible because on the 2nd and 3rd of May the army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina fired several artillery missiles on Zagreb, thereby killing seven civilians and wounding many. The OTP submits that this operation had no military justification. All this was happening at a time when the Serbian Krajina army was no longer able to protect the Serbian civilian population that was being subjected to a severe massacre and the UN were obviously unable to stop this Croatian aggression. This appeared to be the only way to stop the massacre being perpetrated by the Croatian army. Following detailed reports to the United Nations drafted in the first 10 days of May 1995, stating the exact number of those killed and their names, it was established that Serb civilians were massacred who had joined convoys on their way out, and this massacre had been perpetrated by the Croatian authorities. There is an UNPROFOR document indicating that the Croatian authorities were using water tankers and hoses to wash the blood of the Serb civilians off the roads that the Serbs had been massacred on, in order to keep this fact hidden from international observers. These reports are numerous and quite detailed but the OTP does not want to know about these reports. I am the only one to stand indicted here. I, a representative of those Serbian victims. The objective being to hide the massacre. Encouraged by the indictment against me, as soon as 50 days after Operation Flash, with no investigation having been conducted and on account of the fact that none of the Croatian leaders were accused of this brutal aggression and ethnic cleansing of the entire area of Western Slavonia, the Croatian leaders decide to -- decided to complete their plan to entirely destroy the Krajina Serbs. They started on the 4th of August 1995, and Operation Storm began. The entire Croatian army with the cooperation of the Croatian police had seven times the might of the Serbian defence forces. There was renewed aggression, this time under the protection of -- against an area protected by the UN. Within a space of seven days, they occupied the area of north Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun, and Banja. They were given support by the BH army as well as air support by the US Air Force. They used heavy artillery fire to spray the entire territory of Krajina and all its settled areas, villages and towns. According to information provided by UNCRO within a space of 24 hours Knin was targeted with 2500 shells and mortars of different kind, about 30.000 soldiers of the Krajina army were not able to resist this synchronised attack by a force that was seven times as big and as strong. Bitter experience had taught them and there was a huge column of refugees containing more than 200.000 people who were now on their way to Bosnia and Herzegovina looking for salvation. Again, these unprotected and helpless civilians were being pounded by artillery and even bombed by planes as they were about to cross into Bosnia and Herzegovina. The exact number of casualties was never established. More than 1.934 persons are still listed as missing, 524 of whom women, about 1500 members of the Serbian Krajina army survived captivity. About 3200 elderly or disabled people who refused to leave their homes were sent to camps. The Krajina area was devastated, looted, burned, and razed the to the ground. UN military observers in October 1995, and I'm only talking about sector south, recorded as many as 22.000 Serb houses that had been destroyed. What do all these facts show? In the period of time relevant to the indictment, Croatia's Serbs, as an ethnic minority, merely tried to defend themselves from pogrom and from impending genocide. Alas, they failed, despite the presence of UN peacekeeping troops. The true objective of the Croatian authorities was stated in no uncertain terms by the president of the Republic of Croatia, Franjo Tudjman, on the 15th of January 1996, in the Croatian parliament when he said, "Operation Storm has been successfully completed and the main internal problem of the Croatian state has thus been solved." Of course, this must be a reference to Serbs. I'm quoting General Franjo Tudjman, something he said in February 1990 at the founding session of the HDZ about the independent state of Croatia not having been only a quisling creation and a fascist crime but also a true expression of the historical ambition of the Croatian people has thus reached its fruition. The fascist state of NDH had as its ideologue, Dr. Ante Starcevic who was on record as saying that the Serbs were an inferior race and should be struck down with an ax. The NDH, the independent state of Croatia committed a horrible genocide against Serbs between 1941 and 1945. The new Croatian leadership adopted the same ideas and the same policies in order to again commit a genocide against Croatia's Serbs. Today there are as good as no Serbs left in Croatia as a result. In the light of these facts, facts that are no doubt easily available to the OTP, I hope the Defence will succeed in showing that this indictment against me as a high-ranking official of the Republic of Serbian Krajina is entirely inaccurate and unfounded. The indictment reverses the roles of the victim and the perpetrator. The responsibility of Croatia for the breaking up of Yugoslavia, both a historical responsibility and a factual responsibility is beyond doubt. An opportunity came along to commit another genocide against the Serbian population. We from Krajina could not allow that. This trial gives me a chance to present details on the sufferings of my people who have been exiled. Your Honours, I was born in an area where there can be no wheeling and dealing between justice and injustice. I will not be punished by you, since I have already been punished by life itself. It is from Scheveningen that I am watching the injustice done against my people. This is a much more serious matter for me, and much more difficult to cope with than any sentence that will be imposed against me as an individual. God knows I have done my best to protect my people and I have done my best to protect every individual seeking help and protection. Finally, those who know me know full well that I was the first to oppose any wrongdoing or any crime being committed. Thank you. If I may be allowed something outside my opening statement, I do have an objection to make about the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honours, maybe the interpreters are not doing this deliberately but the interpretation I am getting is interpretation in a language that I can only describe as grotesque. When you're receiving interpretation into English, it must be the same thing, I suppose. However, I have taken down a number of words that Pavelic's minister, Mile Budak, invented during the independent state of Croatia. The same words are now being used for my interpretation, the interpretation that I'm receiving. I'm quoting a mere handful of these: "Naputak," meaning "instruction"; "priopcenje," meaning "report" -- just a minute, please. "Potkapak" [phoen] meaning "proof" or "evidence"; "stozer" meaning "headquarters." I don't believe that the interpreters are doing this deliberately. Maybe they were just born at a later time. This language was created by Mile Budak, and was only used by the independent state of Croatia between 1941 and 1945. This language was as if it were re-invented when Franjo Tudjman emerged as the loader of the new Croatian government. I would like to ask the interpreters to please try and take this into account and avoid using these words. There is a language that is still used in Croatia, that used to be valid before all of this happened. That language I do not mind, but these words being used bring a much darker memory to my mind. This is no problem for you because you're getting the same sort of interpretation for both varieties, for both different words used, but I, as a human being, am greatly disturbed by there practice. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Martic. We've heard what you've got to say. I think this brings us to the end of the proceedings for today. It doesn't appear that there is any need for another session tomorrow. The matter will then stand adjourned to the 16th of January 2006, at 3.45 in this courtroom. Court stands adjourned.
